en: Thus have I heard: Majjhima Nikāya 116, the Isigili Sutta. Thus have I heard: [One day the Blessed One was staying near Rājagaha on Mount Isigili.]... [The rest of the sutta follows.]... Thus have I heard.
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha on Mount Isigili.
There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus!”
“Venerable Sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said this:
“Do you see, bhikkhus, that Vebhāra Mountain?”
“Yes, venerable sir.
“Bhikkhus, even for this Vebhāra mountain there was one designation and another description.
Do you see, bhikkhus, that Paṇḍava mountain?”
“Yes, venerable sir.
“Bhikkhus, even for this Mount Paṇḍava there was one designation and another description.
Do you see, bhikkhus, that mountain Vepulla?”
“Yes, venerable sir.
“Bhikkhus, even this mountain Vepulla had another name and another designation.
Do you see, bhikkhus, that mountain Gijjhakūṭa?”
“Yes, venerable sir.
“Bhikkhus, even this Vulture Peak Mountain had another name and another designation.
Do you see, bhikkhus, this mountain Isigili?”
“Yes, venerable sir.
“Furthermore, monks, this was indeed the conventional designation for this Isigili mountain; this was its description.
Once upon a time, monks, five hundred paccekabuddhas lived for a long time on this Isigili mountain.”
As they were entering this mountain, they were seen; once they had entered, they were no longer seen.
When people saw this, they said:
"This mountain is swallowing these seers."
The designation ‘Isigili, Isigili’ indeed arose for it.
Monks, I shall declare the names of the paccekabuddhas;
monks, I shall proclaim the names of the paccekabuddhas.
“Bhikkhus, I will proclaim the names of the paccekabuddhas.
Listen to that and attend closely; I shall speak.
“Yes, venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said this:
“Bhikkhus, a paccekabuddha named Ariṭṭha was a long-time resident on this Isigili mountain;
a paccekabuddha named Upariṭṭha, bhikkhus, was a long-time resident on this Isigili mountain.”
“Monks, the paccekabuddha named Tagarasikhī dwelt for a long time on this Isigili mountain;
the paccekabuddha named Yasassī, monks, dwelt for a long time on this Isigili mountain;
the paccekabuddha named Sudassana, monks, dwelt for a long time on this Isigili mountain.”
“Bhikkhus, the paccekabuddha named Piyaḍassī dwelt for a long time on this Isigili mountain;
the paccekabuddha named Gandhāra dwelt for a long time on this Isigili mountain;
the paccekabuddha named Piṇḍola dwelt for a long time on this Isigili mountain.”
"Monks, the Paccekasambuddha named Upāsabha was a long-time resident on this Isigili mountain;
the Paccekasambuddha named Nīta was a long-time resident on this Isigili mountain;
the Paccekasambuddha named Tatha was a long-time resident on this Isigili mountain."
“Bhikkhus, the Paccekasambuddha named Sutavā dwelt for a long time on this Isigili mountain;
the Paccekasambuddha named Bhāvitatta dwelt for a long time on this Isigili mountain.
Those who are the essence of beings, free from distress and free from longing—”
Each one attained enlightenment for himself;
listen as I proclaim the names of those supreme men who are free from the arrows of defilement.
Ariṭṭha, Upāriṭṭha, Tagarasikhī,
Yasassī, Sudassana, Piyadassī, Susambuddha,
Gandhāra, Piṇḍola, and Upāsabha.
Nīta, Tatha, Sutavā, Bhāvitatta;
Sumbha, Subha, Matula, and the eighth, Athassa;
Megha, Anīgha, and Sudāṭha.
The Paccekabuddhas who have exhausted the tether of existence: Hiṅgu and Hiṅga of great power;
the two Jālini Munis and Aṭṭhaka.
Then there was the Buddha Kosala, and also Subāhu;
Upanemisa, Nemisa, Santacitta,
Sacca, Tatha, Viraja, and Paṇḍita.
Kāḷū, Pakāḷa, Vijita, Jita, Aṅga, Paṅga,
and Guttijita— Passi, abandon the root of suffering, which is clinging to existence.
Aparājita conquered the host of Māra.
The Teacher was Pavattā, Sarabhaṅga, Lomahaṃsa,
Uccaṅgamāya, Asita, and Anāsava.
Manomaya, Mānacchida, and Bandhumā;
Tadādhimutta, Vimala, and Ketumā;
Ketumbharāga, Mātaṅga, and Ariya.
Then Accuta, Accutagāma,
Byāmaka; Sumaṅgala, Dabbila,
Supatiṭṭhita, Asayha, Khemābhirata, and Sorata.
The Sangha is difficult to lead, yet it is victorious;
another sage is Sayha, of incomparable exertion;
Ānanda, Nanda, and Upananda—twelve [in number].
Bhāradvāja, who bore his final body;
Mahānāma, Uttara,
Kesī, Sikhī, Sundara, and Dvārabhāja.
Tissa and Upatissa were those who severed the bonds of existence;
Upasīkhi and Sikhī were those who cut off craving.
Maṅgala was a Buddha, free from passion.
Having cut through the net of craving, the root of suffering,
and being led to the state of peace,
the beautiful Uposatha— truly named— attained that tranquil state.
Jeta, Jayanta, Paduma, and Uppala;
Padumuttara, Rakkhita, and Pabbata;
Mānatthaddha, Sobhita, and Vītarāga.
And Kaṇha the Buddha, whose mind is well-liberated;
these and other beings of great power,
the Paccekabuddhas whose craving for existence has been exhausted.
"Worship those great seers who have transcended all attachments and have attained final Nibbāna— those who are immeasurable.
The sixth discourse, the Isigili Sutta, is concluded.
